title: Microsoft Purview: Priority cleanup to permanently delete Exchange mailbox items under holds (Worldwide)
summary: The roadmap facts, tenant switch, policy-creation command, audit controls, default and licensing are supported. Minor corrections remain: cite the review-set deletion source, remove the checklist's unmatched Relabel instruction, and classify this optional capability as review rather than prepare.

claims.claim: Priority cleanup is a Purview Data Lifecycle Management feature for permanently deleting sensitive Exchange mailbox items.
claims.quote: Use the Priority cleanup feature under Data Lifecycle Management in Microsoft Purview when you need to permanently delete sensitive content from Exchange mailboxes

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Priority cleanup can override retention settings that would retain an item.
claims.quote: despite retention settings that retain the item or eDiscovery holds.

claims.claim: Priority cleanup can override eDiscovery holds.
claims.quote: Although priority cleanup can override eDiscovery holds, the data might already be copied to an eDiscovery review set where it can't be deleted by priority cleanup.

claims.quote: Priority cleanup is rolling out in preview and subject to change.

claims.claim: Items follow the same deletion process and timings.
claims.quote: Items still go through the same deletion process with the same timings to ensure a compliant permanent deletion

claims.claim: Priority cleanup does not require waiting for the retention period to expire or the hold to be released.
claims.quote: there's no need to wait for the retention period to expire or the hold to be released.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: After all required approvals, deleted items cannot be restored by users, admins or Microsoft.
claims.quote: When all the required approvals are complete, items are permanently deleted and cannot be restored by users, by admins, or by Microsoft.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Exchange priority cleanup can override Preservation Lock.
claims.quote: Because the deletion is irreversible and can override existing holds and even Preservation Lock, the process requires multiple approvals, specific roles, and is audited.

claims.claim: Items marked as a record cannot be deleted with priority cleanup.
claims.quote: You can't use priority cleanup for items that are marked as a record or regulatory record.

claims.claim: Items marked as a regulatory record cannot be deleted with priority cleanup.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Priority cleanup does not delete data already copied into an eDiscovery review set.
claims.quote: the data might already be copied to an eDiscovery review set where it can't be deleted by priority cleanup.

claims.claim: Review-set data is deleted only when its eDiscovery case is deleted.
claims.quote: You can't delete items from a review set, and you can't delete review sets from a case. To delete a review set and its data, you must delete the eDiscovery case that contains the review set.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/edisc-review-set-manage to sources for the statement that review-set data can be deleted only by deleting its case.

claims.claim: A mailbox must contain at least 10 MB of data to support priority cleanup.
claims.quote: A mailbox must have at least 10-MB data to support priority cleanup.

claims.claim: Priority cleanup also covers SharePoint.
claims.quote: Although you can use the priority cleanup feature for mailboxes and for files in SharePoint and OneDrive, the typical use cases are different.

claims.quote: Although you can use the priority cleanup feature for mailboxes and for files in SharePoint and OneDrive, the typical use cases are different.

claims.quote: choose whether to permanently delete the matched items as soon as possible or retain them for a specific period and then delete them.

claims.where: front matter: action; Why it matters
claims.claim: The prepare action fits the standard for this optional, medium-risk capability.
claims.quote: action: "prepare"; risk: "medium". Body: "no mailbox content is deleted until a Priority Cleanup Admin creates a policy and the approvers approve it."
claims.fix: Set action to "review": the standard assigns review to optional capabilities that change nothing until an administrator chooses them, and the high-risk new-control exception does not apply to this medium-risk page.

claims.quote: Checklist: "Brief approvers on the Pending cleanups page, on the Relabel option and on which existing retention labels they should choose". Table rows cover the tenant switch, policy creation and audit search, not Relabel.
claims.fix: Replace the At rollout bullet beginning "Brief approvers" with "Brief approvers on the Pending cleanups page." Keep the supported factual description of relabeling in Risk assessment.
